text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGER - GeoDNS anomalies detected (us-east -> eu-west routing). Spike in 5xx and increased tail latency since 08:12 UTC. Auto-failover triggered for some regions. Paging SRE oncall: @aj

aj: Acked. I'm on it. pulling metrics and checking geo routing config.

maria: I can dig into Route53 health checks and weights if needed.

kai: I'll look at Cloudflare DNS logs / propagation.

aj: Quick observation - GA metrics show elevated 502/504 from eu-west edge pools and a jump in DNS NXDOMAIN at certain resolvers. Could be propagation or resolver caching issue.

aj: Running quick dig from my laptop to confirm:
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com A
52.18.12.34
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example.com A
(REFUSED)
```

sam: Hmm Cloudflare returning REFUSED to 1.1.1.1? That suggests Cloudflare rate-limiting or inter-provider issue.

aj: I'm toggling GeoDNS to lower-priority fallback to force traffic to hosted-eu cluster temporarily. Doing a weighted update in Route53 (increase weight eu-west primary to 70%).

maria: Noted. I'm disabling Route53 healthcheck failover for this record to prevent flip-flopping while we stabilize.

support-bot: Notifying top 5 customers in affected regions via status.redwood.ai scheduled message.

aj: Opening AWS support ticket (case 123456789) and Cloudflare NOC ticket (CF-987654). Pasting logs below for provider:
```
Name: api.redwood.example.com
Route53 records: GEO round-robin + healthchecks
Last change: 2026-03-15T07:50:22Z
Symptoms: intermittent NXDOMAIN/REFUSED from specific public resolvers, 5xx from eu-hosted endpoints
```

kai: Cloudflare confirmed they're seeing partial authoritative responses from two POPs and are investigating edge DNS daemon. They've escalated to Level 2.

aj: Immediate mitigation summary: reduced Route53 failover sensitivity, bumped eu weight, temporarily increased TTL to 300s to reduce churn.

maria: Also added a short L7 route-based fallback in our smart-router so calls that hit eu-west 5xx are retried to us-east with low-latency retry. Patch deployed to routing config.

aj: Impact assessment: estimated 12-18% of EU traffic experienced DNS lookup failures causing 5xx for ~20-35 minutes depending on resolver cache. Some customers saw degraded latency but no data loss.

sam: Captured timeline for postmortem:
- 08:12 UTC: Alerts triggered (DNS errors + production 5xx)
- 08:15 UTC: Pager -> aj acknowledged
- 08:22 UTC: Weight adjustment and healthcheck disable
- 08:30 UTC: Routing fallback deployed
- 09:05 UTC: Cloudflare indicates partial mitigation; working on daemon restart in affected POPs
- 09:40 UTC: Metrics returning to normal; closing active mitigation steps

aj: Handoff: @maria will be next oncall for the next 2 hours to monitor any re-propagation or bounce. I've documented actions taken and the provider ticket IDs.

maria: taking handoff. I'll watch DNS resolution graphs and alerts, and coordinate with Cloudflare NOC if they need records or logs.

support-bot: Incident status updated: Investigating -> Mitigating -> Partial Service Restored. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

cloudops: We're requesting CF to provide resolver logs and exact deploy window. Also asking AWS to confirm no Route53 control plane throttles.

aj: Can we draft a short customer note for status page? suggested: "We experienced partial DNS resolution issues affecting EU customers between ~08:12 and ~09:40 UTC. Traffic rerouted and mitigations applied; full service restored. Root cause under investigation with Cloudflare/Route53." Thoughts?

sam: LGTM. Add affected percent and guidance: "If you continue to see issues, flush DNS cache or switch to a different resolver temporarily."

maria: I'll finalize and publish the status update.

aj: Closing notes before handoff: collect DNS probe logs from 8.12-9.45 UTC, save route53 change history, attach Cloudflare ticket updates. Postmortem owner: aj.

maria: Acknowledged. Monitoring. :thumbsup:
